protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; performs the file-09 Key sealed laws pin conversion D-044 routed
summary: The primary attack fails cleanly. The §6 segment hash reproduces exactly at lines 1405-1580, and I checked the delimiters rather than the convenience range: line 1405 is the named heading verbatim, line 1581 is the excluded '## 7.' terminator, no intervening same-or-higher heading breaks the span, and laws 1 through 19 are all inside it, matching the cited property. All five cited digests match live bytes and D-044's adoption at afc0990 is confirmed. I also tested the objection I would most expect to make -- that other file-09 rows are being declined generically without being named, which is the shape of my own C2-D044-01 -- and it does not apply: file 09 carries exactly one whole-document freeze pin and zero blueprint pins, so the rejected alternative has nothing to name. One SHOULD-FIX blocks CONSENT. The entry declares COMPOUND reversibility and then gives the bare overturn of a total-reversibility entry, dropping the restore limb that D-044 -- the act this entry names as its model -- states in one short phrase.

objections.claim: The entry declares compound reversibility and then states an overturn procedure that only a total-reversibility entry could use. The restore limb that makes a compound overturn actionable is absent, and the entry's own named model states it.
evidence: D-046 reads in full: 'Compound after the rewrite lands. Overturn: C-D046.'

Adopted D-044, which this entry names in its decision-type line as its model ('Same extraction rule as D-033 / D-044') and which performed the structurally identical property-pin conversion, reads: 'compound after the rewrite lands. Overturn: C-D044, plus restore of the prior scope clause.'
Adopted D-033 states the same idea the long way: 'total before the MF-6 rewrite lands. After that rewrite, overturn also requires reverting or superseding the rewrite commit.'

By contrast the total-reversibility entries in this corpus use exactly D-046's bare form -- D-041, D-042, D-043 and D-045 all read 'Total. Overturn: C-Dxxx.' So D-046 declares the compound class and then supplies the total-class procedure.
objections.whyItMatters: Compound is precisely the declaration that reverting the commit is not sufficient. D-000 clause 3 requires an overturn procedure as a mandatory element, and for this act the missing limb is concrete: restoring the prior whole-file freeze digest e809d439… as the Key sealed laws source pin. Someone executing an overturn from this text reverts C-D046 and stops. The from-value is recoverable, since clause 1 names it, but it sits in the decision rather than in the procedure that is supposed to carry it.
objections.whyThisSeverity: It is an omission of the substance of a required element, with an exact precedent in the entry's own cited model and a one-phrase remedy. That is the same shape and severity I gave C2-D043-01, where an entry invoked a form and dropped the clause that form exists to carry. It is not a MUST-FIX because nothing stated is false and the class declaration itself is correct.
objections.remedy: Match D-044's form: 'Compound after the rewrite lands. Overturn: C-D046, plus restore of the prior whole-file freeze pin e809d439… as the Key sealed laws source pin.'

whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 6f77cd17eddf2a4d94e09b160737315eb0eb70de497062c86ff8e7bdb9b78114 both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

The attack 'unreproducible §6 segment hash' fails. I extracted lines 1405-1580 of the live freeze with sed and hashed them: bfa71f42fb1e25d7d9556ea7549723b8e91af205147d3cca0d34558e1eba3b5e, exactly the cited value.

I verified the delimiters rather than the convenience range, because D-044's rule -- which this entry adopts -- makes the delimiters the pin. Line 1405 is '## 6. Non-negotiable implementation laws', character for character the heading the entry names. Line 1581 is '## 7. Named non-blocking residuals and parks', a heading of the same level, correctly excluded. Line 1580 is the trailing blank, correctly included per 'intervening blanks included'.

I checked the span is unbroken: no '## ' heading occurs anywhere strictly between 1405 and 1580, so no same-or-higher heading terminates §6 early and the extraction cannot have swallowed or truncated a neighbouring section.

The cited property is actually present in the segment. The claim-matrix row cites '§6 laws **1–19 in full**, including law 3 … and law 11 …', and I enumerated the numbered laws inside 1405-1580: 1 through 19, complete and in order. Nothing the row cites falls outside the pinned segment.

The new pin is consistent with the pins D-044 already wrote against the same section. D-044 pinned freeze §6 law 6 at 1442-1463, law 17 at 1497-1498 and law 19 at 1531-1580; all three ranges sit inside 1405-1580, and law 19's end coincides with §6's end, which is what the rule requires when a law is the last in its section.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all five: file 09 b96f6236…, freeze e809d439…, freeze §6 bfa71f42…, file 08 80fc55d1…, COORD 731d8613…. Each measured by me against live bytes, and the COORD pin is the current post-D-045 value rather than a carried-forward stale one. D-044's adoption at afc0990 is confirmed in git log.

The attack 'other file-09 rows converted' fails, and I tested the stronger form of it too. I enumerated every 64-hex digest in file 09: the whole-document freeze digest occurs exactly once, the blueprint digest zero times, and the remaining digests are instrument pins such as product-dispositions.v1 bbe24527… and operability.v10 9bacbbf4…, which are already-specific citations that adopted D-044 expressly kept in that form. So there is no second whole-document standing pin in file 09 for this entry to have silently left behind, and the rejected alternative 'Also convert other file-09 freeze citations' declines a set that is empty rather than one it should have named. This is the objection I raised as C2-D044-01 and it does not arise here.

The attack 'file 08 edited' fails: clause 2 states it, the file-08 digest matches live, and git reports it unmodified. The attack 'baseline JSON edited' fails the same way -- clause 2 states it and git reports both v1-authority-baseline.json and v1-status-evidence.json unmodified.

The attack 'freeze / blueprint motion' fails: clause 3 states 'No freeze motion. No blueprint', and both files measure unchanged and are clean in git. The freeze in particular must not move, since the whole act depends on its pinned digest.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' fails. SATISFIED occurs twice, both refusals -- the subject line's 'Not SATISFIED' and clause 3's 'No SATISFIED' -- and clause 3 states 'Condition 1 does not discharge. Conditions 2–5 remain. Condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization.'
The attack 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' fails on the same clause; condition 5's monopoly is stated and no implementation authorization is given anywhere.

The MF-6 framing is right for this act and differs correctly from D-044's. D-044 said 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)' because it was declining to touch a register it had no authority over in that commit; D-046 says 'File-09 content change is this D-000-reviewed act (MF-6)', which is the correct statement for an act that does change register content -- this entry IS the MF-6 act, rather than deferring to one.
File 09 is unmodified in git, consistent with the dispatch's statement that it is not edited in this review cycle. Nothing has been pre-applied ahead of adoption.
The entry is single-subject and severable: 'file 09 Key sealed laws standing citation only. Not file 08. Not MEASURED regeneration. Not SATISFIED.'

Recorded as context rather than as a finding, since it is not my subject: my turn-3 note on D-045 landed. That entry's adopted Status line reads 'Turn 3 of 3: CONSENT from both independent reviewers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX', so the gate counts I flagged as dropped from the draft table are carried in the record.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of D-046. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

Whether the §6 segment's CONTENT is correct as law — I verified that laws 1 through 19 are present and that the segment boundaries are right, not that any law says what the claim matrix relies on it to say. That is the row owner's question.

Whether the Key sealed laws row's prose survives the conversion unchanged. The entry converts only the source pin and states the cited property, and file 09 is not edited this cycle, so there is nothing yet to compare. That check belongs to the commit this entry authorizes.

Whether any whole-document freeze or blueprint standing pin exists in a document neither I nor the register's pin-accounting note has swept. I checked file 08 and file 09, the two the D-014 accounting note identifies as holding the six freeze pins; I did not sweep every document in the repository.

Line-range stability under any future freeze motion. The entry is explicit that the delimiters are the pin and the line range is convenience at the pinned digest, which is the correct design; I verified both agree today and did not model what happens to the convenience numbers after the freeze next moves.
Whether the claim matrix's owner accepts this conversion. The entry changes a citation form, not a claim.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256; sed extraction and independent hashing of freeze lines 1405-1580; sed inspection of lines 1405, 1580 and 1581 to test the delimiter rule rather than the convenience range; awk scan for intervening same-or-higher headings and for the numbered laws inside the span; enumeration of every 64-hex digest in file 09 to test whether any second whole-document standing pin exists; awk extraction of adopted D-033's and D-044's reversibility lines as the compound-class precedent; git status across file 08, file 09, freeze, blueprint, both baseline JSONs and COORD

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on one SHOULD-FIX, and the rest of this draft is sound. The hash reproduces, the delimiters hold at both ends, the pinned segment actually contains the property the row cites, and the entry does not overreach: it converts one pin, and I confirmed by enumeration that one pin is all there is to convert in file 09. This act also closes the gap I raised as C2-D044-01, which is worth recording as a completed loop. The objection is that the entry declares compound reversibility and then supplies the overturn line of a total-reversibility entry. D-044, which this entry names as its model and which performed the same kind of conversion, states the missing limb in five words.
